g.text: Why: The run is beyond multimode reach, so OS2 single-mode fibre is used; the optic is then chosen
by optical power budget, not by rated distance alone.
- optic 10GBASE-ZR chosen by power budget (see transceiver decision)
- Cat6a + 10GBASE-T: 36 km > 100 m copper channel limit (IEEE 802.3an)
- OM4 + 10GBASE-SR: 36 km > 400 m reach, a modal dispersion (bandwidth-distance) limit at 850 nm
Would change: Would select OM4 + 10GBASE-SR at ≤ 400 m.
Standards: IEEE 802.3ae / IEEE 802.3 Cl. 52 (10GBASE-SR/LR/ER), ANSI/TIA-568.3-D (fibre, connector
Why: The cheapest optic is chosen whose rated reach covers the distance and whose channel
insertion loss leaves at least the minimum operating margin. The IEEE channel insertion loss
already reserves dispersion penalties, so no extra fixed margin is stacked on top; the operating
margin covers ageing, repairs and dirty connectors.
